title: Daskam 5
description: Cosmic dissolution, the stages of creation, and the Virat form.

stanzas.sanskrit:
व्यक्ताव्यक्तमिदं न किञ्चिदभवत्प्राक्प्राकृतप्रक्षये
मायायाम् गुणसाम्यरुद्धविकृतौ त्वय्यागतायां लयम् ।
नो मृत्युश्च तदाऽमृतं च समभून्नाह्नो न रात्रे: स्थिति-
स्तत्रैकस्त्वमशिष्यथा: किल परानन्दप्रकाशात्मना ॥१॥
stanzas.commentary_en: When Mahapralayam happened, Maya vanished in to Bhagwan Himself. Since Maya was not there, this world also ceased to exist. The three Gunas of Maaya were in equilibrium, preventing any modification. At that time neither death nor liberation existed. Day and night also did not exist. Bhagwan alone remained at that time as the Supreme Bliss Consciousness.

stanzas.sanskrit:
काल: कर्म गुणाश्च जीवनिवहा विश्वं च कार्यं विभो
चिल्लीलारतिमेयुषि त्वयि तदा निर्लीनतामाययु: ।
तेषां नैव वदन्त्यसत्त्वमयि भो: शक्त्यात्मना तिष्ठतां
नो चेत् किं गगनप्रसूनसदृशां भूयो भवेत्संभव: ॥२॥
stanzas.commentary_en: The time or Kaala, Karma, Gunas and Jivas all lay within the Supreme Consciousness of the Lord Vishnu. Vedhas do not declare them as non-existent. If so, then how can they come in to existence again?

stanzas.sanskrit:
एवं च द्विपरार्धकालविगतावीक्षां सिसृक्षात्मिकां
बिभ्राणे त्वयि चुक्षुभे त्रिभुवनीभावाय माया स्वयम् ।
मायात: खलु कालशक्तिरखिलादृष्टं स्वभावोऽपि च
प्रादुर्भूय गुणान्विकास्य विदधुस्तस्यास्सहायक्रियाम् ॥३॥
stanzas.commentary_en: At the end of two prardha kaala, Bhagwan decided to start creation again. With HIS mere glance, Bhagwan brought out the Maya and from it emerged the power of Time, the Karma of Jivas and the nature resulting out of such karmas, helping in the creation of the universe.

stanzas.sanskrit:
मायासन्निहितोऽप्रविष्टवपुषा साक्षीति गीतो भवान्
भेदैस्तां प्रतिबिंबतो विविशिवान् जीवोऽपि नैवापर: ।
कालादिप्रतिबोधिताऽथ भवता संचोदिता च स्वयं
माया सा खलु बुद्धितत्त्वमसृजद्योऽसौ महानुच्यते ॥४॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Bhagwan has Maaya, but are not influenced by it. The scriptures declare Bhagwan as mere witness. Bhagwan takes different forms of Maaya and appear as Jivas. Maaya being aroused by time, projected the principle of Intelligence, which is called Mahat.

stanzas.sanskrit:
तत्रासौ त्रिगुणात्मकोऽपि च महान् सत्त्वप्रधान: स्वयं
जीवेऽस्मिन् खलु निर्विकल्पमहमित्युद्बोधनिष्पादक: ।
चक्रेऽस्मिन् सविकल्पबोधकमहन्तत्त्वं महान् खल्वसौ
सम्पुष्टं त्रिगुणैस्तमोऽतिबहुलं विष्णो भवत्प्रेरणात् ॥५॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Even though this Mahat Tattva is made up of three Gunas, it is predominated by Satva. Hence it recognizes the collective Jivas as macro "I",as cosmic whole and not as individual entities. But the same Mahat Tattva, when predominated by Tamas and Rajas, creates by Bhagwan will the feeling of individual "I" called Aham Tattva.

stanzas.sanskrit:
सोऽहं च त्रिगुणक्रमात् त्रिविधतामासाद्य वैकारिको
भूयस्तैजसतामसाविति भवन्नाद्येन सत्त्वात्मना ।
देवानिन्द्रियमानिनोऽकृत दिशावातार्कपाश्यश्विनो
वह्नीन्द्राच्युतमित्रकान् विधुविधिश्रीरुद्रशारीरकान् ॥६॥
stanzas.commentary_en: This Aham tattva mixed with three gunas to form Satvika or vaikarika, Rajasa, Tamasa ahamkara. The Satvika or the vaikarika ahamkara then created  presiding dieties of Jnanendriyas, which are Dik Devata (of hearing), Vaayu (of touch), Soorya (of seeing), Varuna (of taste) and Ashwini Devatas (of smell). Karmendriyaas - (organs of action) which are Agni (of speech), Indra (of hands), Vishnu (of the legs), Mitra (of excretion) and Prajaapati (of reproduction). Antahkarana -(Inner equipment consisting of Mana, Buddhi, Ahankaara and Chit) which are Moon (of mind), Brahma (of Buddhi- the intellect), Rudra (of Ahamkaara) and Kshetrajna (of Chitt -memory).

stanzas.sanskrit:
भूमन् मानसबुद्ध्यहंकृतिमिलच्चित्ताख्यवृत्त्यन्वितं
तच्चान्त:करणं विभो तव बलात् सत्त्वांश एवासृजत् ।
जातस्तैजसतो दशेन्द्रियगणस्तत्तामसांशात्पुन-
तन्मात्रं नभसो मरुत्पुरपते शब्दोऽजनि त्वद्बलात् ॥७॥
stanzas.commentary_en:
By Bhagwan will, from the Saatvic aspect of Ahankaara, the inner equipment of Antahkarana was born, consisting of, Manas, Buddhi, Ahankaara and Chitta. 
From the Rajasic aspect of the Ahankaara the ten Indriyaas were born (5 Karmendriyaas and 5 Jnanendriyaas). 
From the Tamasic aspect of the Ahankaara was born, the sound (Sabda) which is the subtle essence (Tanmaatra) of space (Aakaash).

stanzas.sanskrit:
शब्दाद्व्योम तत: ससर्जिथ विभो स्पर्शं ततो मारुतं
तस्माद्रूपमतो महोऽथ च रसं तोयं च गन्धं महीम् ।
एवं माधव पूर्वपूर्वकलनादाद्याद्यधर्मान्वितं
भूतग्राममिमं त्वमेव भगवन् प्राकाशयस्तामसात् ॥८॥
stanzas.commentary_en: From the Tanmaatra of (Shabda) the subtle element of sound, came the element (Aakash) Space and from it touch (Sparsh). From it came the element Air (Vaayu) and from it form (Roopa). From it came the element Fire (Agni) and from it Taste (Rasa). From Rasa came the element Water (Jala) and from it smell (Gandha). From it came the element Earth (Bhoomi). Thus from the Tamasic aspect of Ahankaara, were born the five Tanmaatras and the five Pancha Bhootas each element having the qualities of the preceding one.

stanzas.sanskrit:
एते भूतगणास्तथेन्द्रियगणा देवाश्च जाता: पृथङ्-
नो शेकुर्भुवनाण्डनिर्मितिविधौ देवैरमीभिस्तदा ।
त्वं नानाविधसूक्तिभिर्नुतगुणस्तत्त्वान्यमून्याविशं-
श्चेष्टाशक्तिमुदीर्य तानि घटयन् हैरण्यमण्डं व्यधा: ॥९॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Even though all these elements, sense organs , the organs of action, and their presiding deities came into existence, they could not by themselves create the Brahmaanda. Then the presiding deities glorified Bhagwan by various hymns who entered into all of them, activated them and combining them, created the Hiranya Andam (the Golden Egg).

stanzas.sanskrit:
अण्डं तत्खलु पूर्वसृष्टसलिलेऽतिष्ठत् सहस्रं समा:
निर्भिन्दन्नकृथाश्चतुर्दशजगद्रूपं विराडाह्वयम् ।
साहस्रै: करपादमूर्धनिवहैर्निश्शेषजीवात्मको
निर्भातोऽसि मरुत्पुराधिप स मां त्रायस्व सर्वामयात् ॥१०॥
stanzas.commentary_en:
This Brahmaanda remained in the cosmic waters, created by Bhagwan for thousand years. Thereafter, Bhagwan broke the Brahmaanda and took the cosmic form or Viraat Roopa adorned with 14 worlds with thousands of hands, feet, heads  and appeared as collective form of all Jiivatmas.
Bhattathiri prayed to Guruvayoorappan who manifested as Virat Roopam in the beginning of creation to cure him of all his afflictions.
